You control a UR5e robot arm with a parallel gripper in a physics simulator. Your job is to build a target structure out of box-shaped parts that start parked on the table.

Units and frame: all positions are part centers in meters, in the world frame; z is up and the table surface is z = 0. Every part stays upright, so only its center position matters (yaw 0).

The target is given only as images. You are not told the target position of any part; you must infer it.

Tools:
- get_task(): the list of parts (index, size_m [x, y, z]) and images of the finished target structure. The images are orthographic views: a top view (looking down -z, horizontal axis x, vertical axis y), a front view (looking along +y, horizontal axis x, vertical axis z) and a side view (looking along -x, horizontal axis y, vertical axis z). Each view has a metric grid with labeled coordinates in meters, and each part is labeled with its index. The robot arm is not part of the target.
- observe(): the current position of every part, whether it is upright, and the arm/gripper state.
- move_part(part, x, y, z, yaw_deg=0): picks up one part and places it with its center at (x, y, z), then returns the arm home. The planner rejects moves it cannot do safely (no collision-free path, no support under the destination, etc.) and reports why. A failed or bad move can disturb other parts, so observe() after anything unexpected.
- reset_scene(): puts every part back at its parked start. Use it if the scene is ruined. It does not refund the budget.
- run_python(code): runs Python in a scratch directory that contains task.json (part sizes only), state.json and your memory/ folder. Use it for geometry and bookkeeping. It cannot touch the simulator or see the images.
- list_memory(), read_memory(path), write_memory(path, content): a persistent memory/ folder that survives across tasks.
- submit(): ends the episode and scores it. The episode passes only if every part is within 5 mm of its target position, upright, resting on what it should rest on, and the whole structure stays still for one second.

Reading positions off the grid is only approximate. Use the part sizes to make positions exact: a part resting on the table has z = size_z / 2, a part resting on others has its bottom at the top of its supports, and parts that touch in the images usually share an exact edge or center line.

Physics matters: a part can only be placed where something (the table or parts already placed) will support it, and parts placed too early can block later moves. Decide the build order yourself.

At the start of each task, read your memory. Before you submit, write down anything that would help you on future tasks: what worked, what failed and why, and reusable code. Keep notes short and general, not specific to this task's coordinates. The episode also ends if you run out of turns, tokens or time, in which case the current scene is scored as is.

arguments.code:
import json
sizes = {i: [0.02,0.03,0.03] if i in (0,1) else None for i in range(7)}
sizes.update({2:[0.08,0.03,0.01],3:[0.04,0.06,0.01],4:[0.12,0.06,0.02],5:[0.03,0.10,0.02],6:[0.08,0.06,0.02]})

# Build a vertical tower, all centered at y=0, symmetric about x=0.40
# Front view order bottom->top: 0&1 (legs) / 2 (bridge) / 3 / 4 / 5 / 6
# z computed by stacking heights.
targets = {}
# legs on table
targets[0] = (0.37, 0.0, 0.015)
targets[1] = (0.43, 0.0, 0.015)
z = 0.03
for idx in [2,3,4,5,6]:
    h = sizes[idx][2]
    cx = 0.40
    targets[idx] = (cx, 0.0, z + h/2)
    z += h
for i,(x,y,zz) in targets.items():
    print(i, (x,y,zz), "top=", zz+sizes[i][2]/2)

arguments.content:
# Box-stacking task notes

## Reading targets from views
- Front view (x/z) gives x centers + z stacking order (bottom->top).
- Top view (x/y) gives y centers + which parts are hidden under larger ones.
- Side view (y/z) confirms y centers and stacking.
- All positions exact: table z=0 -> resting part center z = size_z/2; stacked part bottom = top of support.
- Symmetric towers: central parts share the same x (symmetry axis), legs symmetric about it.
- 5mm tolerance, so read to ~mm and refine with sizes.

## Build order
- Always bottom-up so each part has support when placed.
- Legs/base first, then bridge, then up the tower.

## Gotchas
- A part spanning two separate supports (bridge): COM must lie inside convex hull of
  contact patches, not just the union. Symmetric bridge = stable. Planner may still
  reject; observe reason.
- Overhanging slabs: stable if COM (center) projects over the smaller support below.
- Place small top parts last; arm approaches from above the narrow tower fine.
- move_part: pick->place->home. observe() after anything unexpected.
